title: AutoSOUP: Safety-Oriented Unit Proof Generation for Component-level Memory-Safety Verification
claim: AutoSOUP derives memory-safety unit proofs (scope, loop bounds, environment models) for C components by running BMC in coverage mode and asking an LLM only to classify why a property line is unreached; on 60 recreated CVEs it exposed 40 (66.7 percent), against 17 for a Codex agent and 25 for the Seeker baseline.
quote: We formalize these unit proofs as artifacts that encode verification choices (scope, loop bounds, and environment models) for verifying safety properties, and introduce three techniques for deriving them automatically.
take: Run CBMC in coverage mode on each native harness, let a model classify only why the property line is unreached (loop bound, missing configuration, side effects of an external call) and apply the matching local repair, replacing hand-set unwind bounds in native_case.py with a coverage-driven bound search that the existing assumption-coverage stage can audit.
falsifier: On the pinned native cases, count harnesses whose hand-set bounds change under the coverage-driven search and whether any control verdict flips; if the search needs more than 3 CBMC runs per case on average or flips one control verdict, it does not help.
gap_note: The sections read do not give the agent prompts, the resource-budget values or the build-configuration recovery in detail; the method starts from entry points with pointer arguments and has no stage for C++ or for scalar-only inputs.

title: Agentic Model Checking
claim: Agentic model checking keeps every soundness-relevant decision in the BMC backend and lets LLM agents do spec inference, check selection, counterexample classification and refinement proposals; witnesses pass four stages (input reachability, callee feasibility with real bodies, dynamic replay under signals, realism audit) and refinements pass a deterministic soundness guard.
quote: agents propose, solvers verify: agents handle tasks requiring semantic judgment (spec inference, check selection, counterexample classification, refinement proposal) while BMC discharges every soundness-relevant decision.
take: Add a callee-feasibility stage to the native gate: re-run CBMC with real callee bodies and the witness inputs pinned, so a counterexample that depends on a hand-written stand-in's return value is labeled stand-in-dependent before native_case.replay compiles it under the sanitizers.
falsifier: On the existing native controls, count counterexamples that rest on a hand-written stand-in; if fewer than 1 case changes label or verdict under the real-body re-run, the stage adds nothing measurable.
gap_note: The results tables were not read, so per-stage rejection counts are unknown; real callee bodies are unavailable for snprintf and ctype under CBMC, which is the case dawnr needs most.

title: Unlocking the Power of Environment Assumptions for Unit Proofs
claim: vMocks give a gMock-inspired expectation DSL (times, returnFn, captureArgAndInvoke, invokeFn) resolved at compile time with C++17 templates for symbolic environments; the authors verify functions of the mbedTLS ssl_msg.c source with SeaMock and SeaHorn.
quote: In our work, we draw inspiration from tMocks and introduce their counterpart in the realm of formal verification, which we term vMocks. vMocks offer an intuitive framework for specifying a plausible environment when conducting code-level formal verification.
take: Describe each hand-written stand-in for snprintf or a ctype function as a short declarative expectation (call count, return function, argument capture) in case.json and generate the C stand-in from it, so the stand-ins that are cross-checked natively stay one reviewable line each.
falsifier: Re-express every existing stand-in in the declarative form; if fewer than 80 percent can be expressed without raw C, the DSL does not cover dawnr's stand-ins.
gap_note: The framework is C++17 template metaprogramming for SeaHorn, not C for CBMC, so the generator and the expectation grammar must be built; the paper's evaluation is one mbedTLS file.

title: Function Contracts for Bounded Model Checking of C Programs
claim: ESBMC's function-contract framework generates an enforce wrapper that snapshots non-assigned globals, assumes the precondition, calls the renamed original and asserts frame compliance and the postcondition; the authors derive when its encoding emits fewer verification conditions than CBMC's, and report that a harness defining reach_error as abort silently dropped the functional property from every run until corrected.
quote: Bounded model checking unrolls a program into a single formula, so a function holding a loop costs the solver a fresh copy of that loop at every call site.
take: Replace a loop-bearing callee in a native harness by a contract wrapper (assume precondition, assert postcondition and frame) proven once, then used at call sites, and add a check that the property assertion is reachable in every run, the defect that wrongly inflated the paper's own first results.
falsifier: On native cases with a loop-bearing callee, if the contract route cuts CBMC's verification conditions by less than 20 percent against the inlined callee, contracts do not help the gate.
gap_note: The implementation and the crossover formula are for ESBMC's snapshot encoding against CBMC's operational (DFCC) encoding, counted in verification conditions and not solver time; the study notes it had to complete benchmark contracts with input bounds that the original requires clauses omitted.

title: Correctness Witnesses with Function Contracts
claim: The paper proposes extending verification witness format 2.0, which today encodes only loop and location invariants as C expressions, with function contracts.
quote: We propose an extension to the existing witness format 2.0 to allow for the specification of function contracts.
take: Let a verified native case emit its assumptions and loop bounds as a witness-style contract that another bounded checker can recheck, instead of recording them only as counts in case.json.

title: Streaming LRAT Certificates into Lean Theorems
claim: lrat-catcher turns a SAT solver's LRAT certificate into a Lean theorem with two import modes; a scaling experiment on the empty-hexagon problem imports 174 TB of certificates through streaming.
quote: We propose the tool lrat-catcher, which turns a certificate into a Lean theorem.
take: Dump the CNF of a verified native case, solve it with a proof-producing solver and check the LRAT certificate through the Lean route, which dawnr already runs as one of its seven systems, so that a small case no longer rests on a trusted solver verdict.

title: The Refutation Gap: Certifying Both Halves of an Optimality Claim
claim: Published minimal XOR circuit counts carry no certificate for either half of the optimality claim; with certificates the median proof is 1.1 MB and checking costs 1.9x solving.
quote: We call this the refutation gap: published gate counts for minimal XOR circuits provide no certificate for either half of the claim, and neither did 121 optimality results we ourselves produced.
take: Use the reported proof size and 1.9x checking cost as the cost model for deciding whether DRAT proofs can be attached to every UNSAT verdict of the native gate, and borrow its wording of a missing refutation certificate as a named limit.

title: Prompt Fuzzing for Fuzz Driver Generation
claim: PromptFuzz iteratively generates fuzz drivers for uncovered library code using instructive program generation, erroneous program validation, coverage-guided prompt mutation and constrained fuzzer scheduling.
quote: To explore API usage in fuzz drivers during prompt fuzzing, we propose several key techniques: instructive program generation, erroneous program validation, coverage-guided prompt mutation, and constrained fuzzer scheduling.
take: Accept a model-drafted harness body only after the native compile succeeds and execution reaches the end marker, the validation step PromptFuzz puts before fuzzing, so that drafts reach CBMC already proved well formed.

title: Understanding Gaps in LLM Pipelines Towards Scalable Fuzzing Harness Generation: An Empirical Study and Enhancement
claim: An empirical study of LLM-based harness generation frameworks over 29 OSS-Fuzz projects, whose findings are applied as a hybrid tool pool for context retrieval, an enhanced validation pipeline and a compilation-error triage strategy.
quote: To answer these questions, we conduct an empirical study on state-of-the-art LLM-based harness generation frameworks across 29 OSS-Fuzz projects.
take: Classify the first native compile failure of a model-drafted case as missing declaration, wrong integer width or prelude gap before retrying, so that repair targets the cause and not the pasted compiler text.

title: Automated Repair of AI Code with Large Language Models and Formal Verification
claim: The authors grow NeuroCodeBench to about 81k programs by mutation, check the mutants' memory safety with ESBMC and ask an LLM to repair the source whenever ESBMC reports a vulnerability.
quote: Whenever ESBMC spots a vulnerability, we invoke a large language model to repair the source code.
take: Keep a model-proposed fix only when the same harness no longer yields a counterexample under CBMC, which matches the fixed-variant control of native_case (original refuted, fixed verified) and yields a repair loop for real findings.

title: SV-LIB 1.0: A Standard Exchange Format for Software-Verification Tasks
claim: SV-LIB is proposed as an exchange format and intermediate language for software-verification tasks, covering programs, specifications and verification witnesses, with expressions and sorts in SMT-LIB.
quote: To address the problem, we propose SV-LIB, an exchange format and intermediate language for software-verification tasks, including programs, specifications, and verification witnesses.
take: Compare the SV-LIB task schema with case.json to see whether a native case could be exported so a second bounded checker returns a verdict on the same case, which would give the single-solver gate an independent reading.

title: Finding Software Vulnerabilities in Open-Source C Projects via Bounded Model Checking
claim: A methodology that pre-processes source files and guides a bounded model checker through them with a function-wise prioritization strategy; the authors report that it can efficiently verify large software systems.
quote: In particular, we pre-process input source-code files and guide the respective model checker to explore them systematically.
take: Rank the functions of a target project by an importance scale before choosing which become native cases, so the scarce finding-to-case effort is spent on functions the checker can reach and that matter.

title: Verified but Vacuous: Three Failure Surfaces of LLM-Driven Verified Code Generation
claim: Separating verifier acceptance, syntactic specification binding and semantic fidelity, the authors report 99.1 percent Dafny verifier acceptance on HumanEval against 1.9 percent with a certificate bound to a spec-defined predicate, and 11.48 and 14.82 percent of structurally verified Rust samples still failing hidden tests.
quote: Many existing pipelines report a single verification number.
take: Add the ensures-binding gate as a pre-solver check in the specification gate: a static walk that rejects an answer unless some postcondition names a specification-defined predicate or function, which would stop acceptances like ensures result >= 0 before any of the seven systems runs.
falsifier: Run the gate over the 1,038 proved training answers and the clean held-out answers; if it rejects fewer than 1 percent of them, or rejects an answer that the Python-solution check in spec_check.py keeps as complete, it adds no discrimination.
gap_note: The gate is defined for Dafny pipelines that emit a separate specification file and implementation; t needs the identifier check on its own syntax tree, and the paper states it misses predicates that are vacuous themselves, such as predicate P(x) { true }.

title: Validating Autoformalized Specifications via Contrapuntal Languages
claim: Pairs of task-specific formal languages with no structure-preserving translation between them are synthesized so that errors in independent formalizations decorrelate; accepted specifications are scored by mutants killed and correctness rate, and error coincidence is compared for same-language pairs against cross-language pairs.
quote: Our key insight is that these errors can be decorrelated through representational diversity.
take: Measure error coincidence across dawnr's lowerings: among pairs of wrong answers, the fraction wrong in the same way, grouped by whether the two lowerings share a parser or a solver, to test whether shared front ends make seven-way agreement weaker than seven independent votes.
falsifier: On the 182 held-out cells, compute error coincidence for lowering pairs that share a front end or solver against pairs that do not; if the two rates differ by less than 5 percentage points, shared front ends are not weakening independence.
gap_note: Language synthesis there is built on SMT-LIB with shape constraints over logical formulas; dawnr's seven systems already differ in logic and would need a measured, not constructed, notion of translations that preserve structure.

title: Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis
claim: DRAGO diagnoses formalization errors deterministically and keeps a model rewrite only if it parses, strictly lowers a diagnostic error weight and does not regress solver status; LLM-only diagnosis caused regressions in 11.8 percent of initially correct specifications.
quote: Purely LLM-based diagnosis, lacking a formal ground truth, often fails to spot these errors, and its ungrounded critiques cause regressions in 11.8% of initially correct specifications in our experiments.
take: Gate every model repair by an evidence-gated acceptance predicate (well formed, diagnostic weight strictly falls, no regression of any kernel verdict) before it replaces the original answer, so the proof and specification repair routes cannot lose a kernel the way two answers did in the witness-fed repair run.
falsifier: Replay the 182-cell repair run with the predicate in place; if either of the 2 answers that lost a kernel is still replaced, or the net gain falls below the 69 of 182 cells reached without it, the predicate does not help.
gap_note: The deterministic diagnostics are written for first-order logic, PDDL and optimization formalizations; a diagnostic weight and a list of blocking findings for t programs must be defined first.

title: How Stable Are LLM-Generated Proofs Under Program Refactoring? A Stress Test for Verifiable Code Generation
claim: RefactorProof derives 458 Lean-certified variants from 185 VERINA tasks using five rewrites (let introduction, helper extraction, operand swap, conditional inversion, branch extraction); it reports a proof survival rate per source and that a predefined one-identifier edit repairs 109 of 139 structural failures with a median two-token edit.
quote: We introduce RefactorProof, which derives 458 Lean-certified variants from the 185 VERINA tasks that compile in our pinned environment while holding the specification and evaluated proof fixed byte-for-byte.
take: Measure a proof survival rate for each of the seven lowerings under semantics-preserving rewrites of t programs, and try the paper's mechanical one-identifier repair of failed proofs before any model repair is attempted.
falsifier: If the survival rate of every lowering's proof on rewritten t programs is 95 percent or higher, or the mechanical repair fixes fewer than 30 percent of the failures, stability probing is not worth adding to the gate.
gap_note: The study is Lean 4 on 185 VERINA tasks with Lean-specific unfold and simp edits; its five rewrites are written at Lean source level so t-level rewrites must be defined, and specialized provers reached only 13.8 to 16.4 percent coverage at five attempts.

title: Are LLM-Generated Formal Specifications Faithful to Their Requirements? A Study on Bimodal Formal Specification Generation
claim: An empirical study of LLM ACSL specification generation on a benchmark of 1,403 C programs checked with Frama-C, under a setting where the code's correctness is unknown.
quote: Therefore, we conduct an empirical study of LLM-based specification generation under the bimodal setting: given both the natural language requirement and its corresponding code implementation, whose correctness is unknown.
take: Adopt the four-way label of a specification against an incorrect implementation (correct, wrong, misled, weak) for dawnr's accepted answers, with labels derived from tests and validated against a human sample of 50, to split the gate's 0.682 precision into misled and weak shares.
falsifier: If automated and human labels on 50 sampled accepted specifications agree with Cohen's kappa below 0.5 (the paper reports 0.51 to 0.57 before excluding unclassified cases), the automated taxonomy cannot be used to tune the gate.
gap_note: The specifications are ACSL for C functions checked with E-ACSL runtime assertions at calibrated thresholds, and the Other class stays large (13 of 50 for one model); t specifications need their own executable form and thresholds.

title: Beyond LLM Judge: Mechanical Verification for Agentic Autoformalization
claim: A method for verifying Lean formalizations mechanically instead of with an LLM judge reaches the lowest accepted-error rate (incorrect statements accepted) among the evaluated methods on three labeled datasets.
quote: We introduce a novel method for verifying Lean formalizations that goes beyond LLM-judged faithfulness.
take: Report the accepted-error rate, the fraction of wrong statements a check lets through, for dawnr's specification gate alongside precision, since the gate sits at 0.682 precision against a required 0.70.

title: From Natural Language to Verified C: Verification-Guided Generation with ACSL Specifications
claim: VeriGen-C is a framework for joint synthesis of C programs and ACSL specifications from natural-language requirements, generating under verification guidance.
quote: This paper introduces VeriGen-C, a formal-verification-friendly framework for the joint synthesis of C programs and ACSL specifications from natural-language requirements.
take: Compare its joint program-and-ACSL synthesis against dawnr's t-to-Frama-C lowering on the same problems, to see whether requiring the model to emit ACSL directly closes any of the parse wall at the Frama-C backend.

title: Constrained Decoding Eliminates Structural Failures in Small LLMs but Reveals a Scale-Dependent Semantic Gap
claim: Across five 0.6B to 4B models and 14 structured-output tasks, constrained decoding (Outlines, XGrammar) lifted schema validity from 78.6-92.9 percent to 100 percent, while content accuracy kept a scale-dependent gap: type-coercion failures were rescued, instruction-semantic failures such as a missing second function call were not.
quote: Schema conformance is necessary but not sufficient for semantic correctness; CD's reach ends exactly where schema conformance ends.
take: Score every Cohere schema-restricted reply on two axes, structural validity and problem-test agreement, and read a rise in validity without a rise in covered problems as the hollow rescue the paper describes, where a list skeleton passes the schema with no content.
falsifier: On the proposed 50-problem typed-schema pilot, if static-valid completions reach 90 percent but fewer than 5 problems become newly covered, schema restriction fixed structure only and does not help coverage.
gap_note: The tasks are hand-designed JSON extraction and function calling with dense models of 4B parameters or less; there is no code or expression-tree schema, and the hollow rescue is illustrated by one example rather than counted.

title: The Parser Already Knows: Lightweight Bias Correction in Constrained Decoding
claim: SHIM learns a lightweight correction (a logistic regression on grammar-state features and the candidate token) that re-weights grammar-constrained decoding toward the language model's own distribution conditioned on the grammar, implemented on SynCode with a second text-to-SQL domain.
quote: However, because masking only checks whether each token is valid so far, the resulting distribution over complete outputs diverges from the LM's own distribution conditioned on the grammar, biasing generation toward valid but suboptimal outputs.
take: Fit a small logistic correction on t grammar-state features and the candidate token, applied to the mask at each step, to test whether masked decoding's distortion toward valid but wrong programs is part of why constrained decoding raised parsing twofold but test-passing only 1.23x.
falsifier: Rerun the 30B APPS constrained arm with the correction; if test-passing stays below the preregistered 1.5x (1.23x was measured), or parsing falls under its earlier twofold gain, distortion was not the limit.
gap_note: The paper's training data, feature set and models are for Lark grammars under SynCode; the feature set must be rebuilt for t's grammar and a training corpus of valid t prefixes must be assembled from audited problems.

title: AGDecode: Semantic Attribute Grammar Derivatives for Safety-Constrained Decoding of Large Language Models
claim: AGDecode compiles semantic specifications into relational constraints over partially built syntax trees, discharged by SMT and CHC oracles, with soundness and completeness relative to an ideal oracle mechanized in Rocq.
quote: We present AGDecode, a programmable framework for semantic constrained decoding based on least-fixed-point semantics.
take: Express t's scope and type rules as attribute-grammar constraints checked during decoding, so a partial expression with an out-of-scope name or a mismatched operand type is rejected at the token that introduces it, the same constraints the signature-built schema is meant to carry.

title: Trie Automata for Constrained Decoding over Large Finite Sets
claim: The trie automaton uses Aho-Corasick multi-pattern matching to precompute per-node token masks for selection from a finite set of valid strings, reporting 7X faster per-step valid-token computation.
quote: We introduce the trie automaton, a specialized mechanism that exploits finite-set structure (shared prefixes, bounded depth, known cardinality) via Aho-Corasick multi-pattern matching to precompute per-node token masks.
take: Encode the set of in-scope names for a problem's signature as a trie automaton with precomputed per-node masks, so identifier slots in generated t can be restricted to that finite set without recompiling a whole grammar for each problem.

title: Pre$^3$: Enabling Deterministic Pushdown Automata for Faster Structured LLM Generation
claim: Pre3 converts LR(1) grammars into deterministic pushdown automata to cut runtime overhead of context-dependent token processing in constrained LLM decoding, especially under large batches.
quote: To address these issues, we propose Pre$^3$ that exploits deterministic pushdown automata (DPDA) to optimize the constrained LLM decoding efficiency.
take: Time mask construction per token for t's grammar under the current engine against a deterministic-PDA build on the laptop path, to see whether mask computation is a visible share of the cold-start and per-token cost.

title: Flexible and Efficient Grammar-Constrained Decoding
claim: A new grammar-constrained decoding algorithm offers 17.71x faster offline preprocessing than existing approaches while keeping state-of-the-art efficiency in online mask computation.
quote: We present a new GCD algorithm together with an implementation that offers 17.71x faster offline preprocessing than existing approaches while preserving state-of-the-art efficiency in online mask computation.
take: Use fast offline mask preprocessing to build one mask set per problem signature rather than one global grammar, which makes per-problem grammars affordable inside the teacher generation loop.

title: Future Validity is the Missing Statistic: From Impossibility to $Φ$-Estimation for Grammar-Faithful Speculative Decoding
claim: The authors show that a speculative decoder with local mask access, Leviathan rejection and rollback soundness samples from the locally projected distribution and not the grammar-conditional distribution.
quote: We show that any speculative decoder with local mask access, Leviathan rejection, and rollback soundness samples from the locally projected distribution $μ^{\mathrm{proj}}$ rather than the grammar-conditional distribution $μ^\star$.
take: Estimate the future-validity probability on a sample of t prefixes to check whether any speculative or mask-only path in dawnr samples from the projected rather than grammar-conditional law before relying on its accepted-answer rates.

title: No More Import Errors: Constrained Decoding for Guaranteed Valid Imports in LLM-Generated Tests
claim: Constrained Beam Decoding with Lookup guarantees import validity in LLM test generation while avoiding import streaks, repetitive valid imports that exhaust the token budget.
quote: We propose Constrained Beam Decoding with Lookup (CBDL), a novel method that guarantees import validity while addressing import streaks by avoiding premature commitment to tokens that lead to repetitive imports.
take: Scan dawnr's constrained runs for degenerate repetition of valid tokens that uses up the output budget before a program ends, the failure the paper names import streaks, and add the lookup-based avoidance if any appear.

title: Constraint Tax in Open-Weight LLMs: An Empirical Study of Tool Calling Suppression Under Structured Output Constraints
claim: Controlled experiments across model families reproduce Tool Suppression under joint tool-calling and structured-output constraints, while each capability works when evaluated alone.
quote: Through controlled experiments across multiple model families and deployment settings, we consistently reproduce Tool Suppression under joint constraints, while tool execution and schema compliance remain functional when evaluated independently.
take: Run the local assistant's tool-call prompts with and without a schema constraint on the reply and count calls made, to see whether adding structure suppresses tool use in the tool-check evaluation.

title: Constrained Decoding: Harmful or Beneficial? Revisiting Its Impact on LLM Performance
claim: The authors show theoretically that appropriate constraints can preserve or improve performance by eliminating invalid paths, and report that the impact depends on the type of constraint and the output space it removes.
quote: These findings show that the impact of constrained decoding depends on the type of constraint and the output space it removes.
take: Run syntax-only, type and scope constraints as separate arms and report each by the output space it removes, instead of one constrained-versus-free comparison, so the earlier 1.23x is attributed to a constraint type.

title: JSONSchemaBench: A Rigorous Benchmark of Structured Outputs for Language Models
claim: JSONSchemaBench is an evaluation framework for constrained decoding along efficiency, coverage of diverse constraint types and quality of the generated outputs.
quote: We present an evaluation framework to assess constrained decoding approaches across three critical dimensions: efficiency in generating constraint-compliant outputs, coverage of diverse constraint types, and quality of the generated outputs.
take: Pass the proposed signature-built schemas through its coverage check first to list constructs an engine silently drops, and report the pilot on its three axes.

title: Statically Contextualizing Large Language Models with Typed Holes
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Programming Languages, Volume 8, 2024; Issue OOPSLA2 A
claim: Integrating LLM code generation into the Hazel typed-hole environment, the authors find on their MVUBench dataset that contextualization with type definitions is particularly impactful.
quote: We find that contextualization with type definitions is particularly impactful.
take: Put the declared types and in-scope definitions around the target hole into the prompt for each t problem before any schema is applied, to test the finding that type definitions are the most useful context.

title: Metamodel-Guided LLM Decoding for Consistent DSL Generation
claim: MeMoDecode enforces a DSL's concrete syntax, abstract syntax and well-formedness constraints jointly during decoding.
quote: We present MeMoDecode: a decoding framework that enforces a DSL's concrete syntax, abstract syntax, and well-formedness constraints jointly.
take: Move the well-formedness rules now checked after a reply completes in check_wf into the decoding step as a third layer above syntax and types.

title: Specification-Guided Generation for Large Language Models
claim: A neuro-symbolic specification-guided decoding framework combines LLM generation with symbolic reasoning to enforce a formal specification, not only syntax.
quote: Large language models (LLMs) can generate structured outputs, but existing constrained-decoding methods mainly enforce syntax and cannot directly enforce satisfaction of a formal specification.
take: Prune partial postconditions during decoding by symbolic checks against the problem's own tests, so that a specification which the later spec_check would reject is never completed.

title: Schema-Key Wording as an Instruction Channel in Structured Generation under Constrained Decoding
claim: On GSM8K and Math500 across seven models, changing only schema-key wording substantially affects accuracy under constrained decoding, with positive and negative effects across models.
quote: Experiments on GSM8K and Math500 across seven language models show that changing only schema-key wording can substantially affect accuracy, with both positive and negative effects across models.
take: Run the schema pilot twice, with neutral field names and with instruction-bearing field names, because key wording acts as a hidden prompt under constraint.

title: Try Again, Don't Look Back: Blind Resampling Outperforms Self-Repair in Small Code Models
claim: On MBPP+ at 1.5B, 3B and 7B, blind resampling gave the highest pass rate at 1.5B and 3B and was indistinguishable from the best condition at 7B; real execution feedback was not distinguishable from a content-free failure notice, and conditions that show the model its own failed program reproduced near-identical code more often.
quote: Using a placebo-controlled design on MBPP+ at three model scales (1.5B, 3B, 7B), we compare four matched-budget retry conditions: blind resampling, a content-free failure notice, genuine execution feedback, and feedback augmented with verbal self-reflection.
take: Add the four-condition decomposition (blind resample, content-free failure notice, real witness, witness plus prose diagnosis) at equal request budget to the planned repair diagnostic, so it is known whether the witness text or only the extra draw moved the seven-way gate from 66 to 69 of 182 cells.
falsifier: On the frozen diagnostic split drawn from training-side problems, if blind resampling at equal request budget repairs within 2 problems of witness-fed repair and regresses none, the witness content is not what helps.
gap_note: Function-level Python on one benchmark family with models up to 7B and lexical retrieval; no formal-verification witness is involved, so the content-free placebo for a failed proof or refuted twin has to be defined.

title: Falsification, Not Exposure: An Internally Preregistered Placebo-Controlled Decomposition of Self-Repair Feedback in Frozen Small Code Models
claim: On 290 dead task-cell units (no best-of-8 candidate passing the public tier) with three 0.5B-1.5B frozen models, blind resampling beat bare-code retry by 18 net unlocks, code plus executable facts beat a generic-bullet placebo by 15, an instruction-only effect was not distinguishable, and code-plus-facts and blind resampling tied at 26 unlocks each.
quote: Across six HumanEval+/MBPP+ cells with three 0.5B-1.5B frozen models, 290 dead task-cell units (no best-of-8 candidate passing the public tier) were evaluated; the main run produced 7,000 fresh generations and a preregistered follow-up 1,400 more.
take: Restrict the repair diagnostic to dead units, those with no sampled clean candidate, and compare four arms at matched generation budget: blind resample, bare retry, code plus witness facts, and a shape-matched content-free placebo, using discordant-pair tests on unlocked problems.
falsifier: On the dead units among the 200 held-out problems, if code plus witness facts unlocks fewer than 3 more problems than blind resampling at equal generation budget (the paper found a tie at 26 each), witness content does not beat extra draws.
gap_note: Python tests with frozen models of 0.5B to 1.5B, 'facts' are executable counterexamples to code, dead units are defined by best-of-8 on public tests; proof witnesses and twin refutations need an equivalent fact format and a matched placebo.

title: Form, Not Content? A Preregistered, Placebo-Controlled Evaluation of Learned Error-Conditioned Self-Repair Through Prompts and Weights in Frozen Small Code Models
claim: PoPE treats a failed program as a conjecture and an execution counterexample as an oracle-relative refutation, and measures with preregistered placebo controls whether the model can use that evidence operationally.
quote: We treat a failed program as a conjecture and an execution counterexample as an oracle-relative refutation, and introduce PoPE (Popperian Placebo-controlled Evaluation): a methodology for measuring whether evidence that falsifies LLM-generated code can be used operationally by that same model.
take: Write the placebo arm into dawnr's next repair preregistration: the same prompt with the witness replaced by a content-free statement that the answer is wrong, scored on the same cells, with the number that would count as no effect stated before the run.

title: Rethinking Self-Repair in Code-as-Policy Agents: What Drives Retry Success?
claim: On the same 252 initial failures Qwen2.5-Coder-7B recovers 85.3 percent within five retries with execution feedback, against 68.3 percent for resampling with the same retry cap.
quote: On the same 252 initial failures, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B recovers 85.3% within five retries, compared with 68.3% for resampling with the same retry cap.
take: Treat this as the opposing result to the placebo studies when reading the repair diagnostic: it studies code-as-policy agents with a retry cap, so dawnr should state which regime its witnesses resemble before choosing between resampling and feedback.

title: Escaping the Self-Repair Trap: Improving Test Oracle Generation via Dual-Context Awareness
claim: Iterative repair of regression oracles is reported to drift toward assertions that are easier to satisfy but less effective at detecting faults, which the authors call the Self-Repair Trap.
quote: Such misalignment biases the repair process, giving rise to a feedback-driven degeneration that we term the Self-Repair Trap, where iterative repair progressively drives models toward assertions that are easier to satisfy but less effective at detecting faults.
take: Log, for each accepted round of specification repair, how many mutants the specification now lets survive, and stop the loop when the kill rate falls, because a repair that weakens the specification passes the gate by lowering it.

title: From Base Rollouts to RL Reasoning: A Budgeted Search Perspective
claim: On Qwen2.5-7B the BOPTR rule approximates the RL default-policy curve from Base operating points with a transfer error of 3.41 percentage points (95 percent interval 2.32 to 5.53), and 3.07 plus or minus 0.39 across three seeds.
quote: On Qwen2.5-7B, BOPTR gives the lowest transfer error among the non-oracle rules we test, 3.41 pp (95% CI [2.32, 5.53]); a three-seed replication gives 3.07 $\pm$ 0.39 pp.
take: Fit the same kind of base-operating-point curve to dawnr's graded sets on disk to see how much of a trained student's gain a larger sample budget reproduces, before another training round is planned.

title: There Is No Free Lunch in RLVR: Every pass@1 Gain Has a pass@k Price
claim: Modeling RLVR as an exponential tilt of a base policy over strategies shared across prompts, the authors prove that every update raising pass@1 lowers some prompt's success under exclusive specialization, that the hardest-prompt loss forces a pass@k crossover whose crossing count is bounded by the sign variation of the per-prompt shift, and give a diagnostic reading the price from an evaluation log.
quote: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) makes a language model solve more problems on the first try and fewer when given many tries: it raises pass@1 while the base model overtakes it at large sampling budget k.
take: Run the paper's log diagnostic on the graded sets of the base and trained student: count sign changes of per-prompt success shift across the 200 held-out problems and read off whether a pass@k crossover exists before any reinforcement round or any change to the ask budget.
falsifier: If the per-prompt success shift between base and trained student shows fewer than 1 sign change over the 200 held-out problems, the pass@k price is not binding for dawnr and reinforcement cannot be blamed for a flat many-sample curve.
gap_note: The theorems assume exclusive specialization and fine coverage and model RLVR updates; dawnr's student is trained by supervised fine-tuning, so whether the tilt model applies must be checked, and the diagnostic needs per-prompt logs at several k.

title: The Reasoning Boundary Paradox: How Reinforcement Learning Constrains Language Models
claim: The authors report a winner-take-all effect in which RLVR reinforces problems that are already likely under the base model while suppressing initially low-likelihood ones.
quote: Second, we uncover the winner-take-all phenomenon: RLVR disproportionately reinforces problems with high likelihood, correct solutions, under the base model, while suppressing other initially low-likelihood ones.
take: After any reinforcement round on the student, list the problems that the base model solved at low rates and that the trained model now never solves, to catch suppression that a single pass@1 figure hides.

title: SCAFFOLD-CEGIS: Preventing Latent Security Degradation in LLM-Driven Iterative Code Refinement
claim: For GPT-4o, 43.7 percent of ten-round iteration chains contained more vulnerabilities than the baseline, and cross-model experiments show the effect is common; SCAFFOLD-CEGIS is proposed against it.

take: Audit each repair chain against round zero: record whether any kernel verdict at round n is worse than at round 0 and cap the number of rounds at the point where chains begin to regress.

title: LeDex: Training LLMs to Better Self-Debug and Explain Code

quote: Intuitively, we observe that a chain of explanations on the wrong code followed by code refinement helps LLMs better analyze the wrong code and do refinement.
take: Build a variant of the 525 existing repair rows with an explanation of why the witness fails placed before the corrected program, keeping only rows whose corrected program passes the strict checks, and compare it with the current rows at equal token count.

title: Counterexample Guided Learning in the Large using Reasoning Agents

take: Use a domain where the verifier is exact, as the paper does, as a calibration for dawnr's witness-fed loop: if counterexamples help the small model here but not on t programs, the limit is in the witness format and not in the model.

title: The Illusion of Safety: Multi-Tier Verification of AI vs. Human C++ Code
claim: VULBENCH-CPP is a benchmark of 8,918 C++ programs from three open-weight LLMs and human authors across 851 competitive-programming tasks, verified in multiple tiers for memory safety.

take: Use its several verification tiers over the same C++ programs as a template for stating where the CBMC gate stands against sanitizer and fuzz tiers on C++ functions the gate cannot take yet; its programs are written by Gemma, Llama and Qwen models, so it is a method to learn from and not training data.

title: ESBMC v7.6: Enhanced Model Checking of C++ Programs with Clang AST
claim: ESBMC v7.6, built on the v7.3 Clang-based C++ front end, is reported to handle a significantly broader range of C++ features from recent versions of the standard.

take: Check which of the Clang-AST C++ features ESBMC v7.6 supports cover the C++ functions in the PX4 sources, as a route to a first C++ native case and a second engine beside CBMC, which has no case for C++ at all.

take: Use the survey's account of ESBMC's evolution to decide which of its features, such as the C++ front end, contracts or interval analysis, are worth an adapter beside CBMC, and record them in the native gate's plan.

title: Using LLMs to Adjudicate Static-Analysis Alerts with Error Reduction Techniques
claim: For adjudicating static-analysis alerts the authors combine a consistency check that reruns the LLM and requires agreeing verdicts with an LLM reasoning evaluation step that picks a verdict after weighing each run's reasoning.

title: FalseCrashReducer: Mitigating False Positive Crashes in OSS-Fuzz-Gen Using Agentic AI

title: SyzHarness: Patch-Based Kernel Bug Reproduction with LLM-Synthesized Fuzzing Harnesses
claim: On 100 KernelCTF cases SyzHarness reproduces bugs with a 78 percent success rate, and on the SyzDirect benchmark with 73 percent, from patch-based harness synthesis.

title: Symbolic Execution Meets Multi-LLM Orchestration: Detecting Memory Vulnerabilities in Incomplete Rust CVE Snippets
claim: The authors address the incomplete-code problem, in which CVE entries give isolated snippets without struct definitions, imports or manifests so that formal verification tools fail at compilation with zero output.

take: Let a model complete missing struct definitions and includes into a prelude for a snippet, and require the native compile to succeed before CBMC is run, so incomplete real-world code can enter the case format.

title: Understanding Formal Reasoning Failures in LLMs as Abstract Interpreters
claim: The paper focuses on abstract-interpretation-based reasoning for invariant generation, introduces two prompting strategies to elicit it from LLMs, and evaluates them on 22 SV-COMP programs.
quote: In this work, we focus on abstract interpretation based-reasoning for invariant generation and introduce two novel prompting strategies that aim to elicit such reasoning from LLMs.
take: Compare model-proposed loop invariants from such prompts against dawnr's hand-set loop bounds on the native cases, to see whether the model can state a bound the assumption-coverage stage then confirms.

title: Verifiers in the Loop: Decoding Time Verification for Code Translation
claim: DTV is a deterministic state-machine controller that at structural boundaries chooses among Generate, Verify, Commit, Rollback, Feedback and Terminate, running deterministic oracles on the rendered prefix; on cost-matched C-to-Rust and JavaScript-to-TypeScript grids it reports a more favorable pass-rate versus token-cost tradeoff than post-hoc verification or sampling-based scaling.
quote: We introduce Decoding Time Verification (DTV), a framework that treats structural boundaries as meta steps for verifier-guided decoding.
take: At each statement boundary of a t program being generated, run the parser and static check on the prefix and roll back to the last committed statement on failure, which turns the post-hoc syntax gate into a per-statement gate at the place where the parse wall arises.
falsifier: On the 200 held-out problems, count answers that end parse-clean under per-statement rollback against post-hoc checking at equal generated tokens; if the parse-clean count rises by fewer than 10 answers, the controller does not move the wall.
gap_note: Its oracles are rustc and tsc on renderable prefixes, so a t prefix needs a defined renderable form; the appendix lists non-local semantic errors, verifier wall-clock cost and a fixed recovery policy as limits.

title: Strategically Diverse Sampling for Self-Training
claim: Sampling responses that commit to different approaches first (Verbalized Sampling, and the hierarchical Groot) gave self-training data on which Qwen3-4B trained on strategically diverse but incorrect traces outperformed IID distillation from a 235B teacher.

take: In the teacher loop sample K distinct approaches per problem (an enumerated list of approaches, then one solution per approach) instead of K independent samples, so the rows that pass all seven systems differ in strategy rather than repeating the one the teacher favors.
falsifier: On the 50 uncovered training problems, if approach-diverse sampling yields fewer than 5 more strict problems than independent sampling at equal request count, diversity is not what limits coverage.
gap_note: Experiments use Qwen3-4B on competitive programming and next-chapter prediction with no formal verifier; dawnr keeps only verified rows so the incorrect-trace result does not transfer, and the Groot procedure was read only in outline.

title: ChopChop: a Programmable Framework for Semantically Constraining the Output of Language Models
claim: ChopChop constructs constrained decoders from an analysis of the space of programs a prefix represents, as the first programmable framework for semantic constraints such as type safety and program invariants.
quote: ChopChop introduces a principled way to construct constrained decoders based on analyzing the space of programs a prefix represents.
take: Compute for each prefix of a t program the set of programs it can still become and drop tokens whose completions cannot be well typed or in scope, using ChopChop's prefix-space analysis as the formal basis for dawnr's prefix automata.

title: Grammar-Based Code Representation: Is It a Worthy Pursuit for LLMs?
claim: The authors develop billion-scale GrammarCoder models that incorporate grammar rules in the code generation process to test whether grammar-based representations pay off at scale.
quote: To explore this, we develop a series of billion-scale GrammarCoder models, incorporating grammar rules in the code generation process.
take: Train locallm on sequences of t production-rule identifiers instead of characters on a small sample, to see whether the parse wall disappears by construction and what happens to test-passing.

title: Fast Controlled Generation from Language Models with Adaptive Weighted Rejection Sampling
claim: The authors replace token masking in locally constrained decoding, which can require evaluating the constraint on every token of a vocabulary above 100,000, with adaptive weighted rejection sampling.

take: Evaluate an expensive constraint, such as a type check on the partial program, only on the sampled token and resample on rejection with a weight correction, instead of masking the full vocabulary at every step.

title: Agnostics: Learning to Code in Any Programming Language via Reinforcement with a Universal Learning Environment
claim: Agnostics is a language-agnostic post-training pipeline that eliminates per-language engineering for learning to code in low-resource languages, using a unified verifier.

take: Pose each problem as input and output over stdin and score the model's t program with one run command, the way nl_stdin tasks already work, so the same reward path serves t without per-language harness code.

title: X-Coder: Advancing Competitive Programming with Synthetic Tasks, Solutions, and Tests
claim: X-Coder examines whether synthetic tasks, verified solutions and reliable test cases can support the full SFT-to-RL cycle for competitive programming with no real-world tasks, solutions or tests used directly.
quote: In this paper, we examine whether synthetic training artifacts can support the complete SFT-to-RL cycle for competitive programming: no real-world tasks, solutions, or test cases are directly used for post-training.
take: Compare its procedure for turning synthetic tasks into reliable test cases with dawnr's test-reliability checks; its generator models are not identified in the text read, so this is a method to learn from and not data.

title: TailSFT: Filtered Fine-Tuning Improves Post-Training Performance
claim: On OLMo-3 7B, TailSFT often improves pass@16 on math and coding evaluations, with gains up to 17 percent absolute, at minimal computational overhead.
quote: On OLMo-3 7B, TailSFT often improves pass@16 performance on math and coding evaluations, with gains up to 17% absolute, while incurring minimal computational overhead.
take: Run its lightweight diagnostic on dawnr's filtered rows before a post-training round to see whether the setting is one where filtered fine-tuning helps at the sixteen-sample level.

title: FGIT: Fault-Guided Fine-Tuning for Code Generation
claim: FGIT extracts line and token level differences between correct and incorrect yet similar implementations to identify error-sensitive segments, and prioritizes those segments with dynamic loss weighting during fine-tuning.
quote: extracting multi-granularity (line/token-level) differences between correct and incorrect yet similar implementations to identify error-sensitive segments, and (2) dynamically prioritizing those segments during training via dynamic loss weighting.
take: Use the token differences between each program and its deliberately broken twin as loss weights, since dawnr already holds a correct and a similar incorrect version of every program.

title: An AI Approach to Verified Production Cryptographic Libraries
claim: CryptoProver synthesizes internal specifications and Verus-checked proofs from high-level API contracts, constructs a new independent proof of curve25519-dalek without changing executable code, and verifies RustCrypto's chacha20 against an RFC 8439 specification.
quote: We present CryptoProver, an AI-based system that synthesizes internal specifications and Verus-checked proofs from high-level API contracts.
take: Read its way of deriving internal lemmas from an API-level contract as a reference for the Verus lowering's lemma generation, and compare which proof obligations it needed that t's lowering emits automatically.

title: Reducing Hallucinations in LLM-Generated Code via Semantic Triangulation
claim: Semantic triangulation decorrelates model errors by turning the problem into a dissociative variant that likely needs a fundamentally different algorithm and checking consistency between independently sampled solutions to both problems.
quote: We introduce semantic triangulation, a theory-grounded framework that decorrelates model errors by transforming the original problem into a dissociative variant - one likely requiring a fundamentally different algorithm - and checks consistency between independently sampled solutions to both problems.
take: For a clean answer, also solve a dissociated variant of the problem and test whether the two solutions agree on shared inputs, as an additional signal where the answer's specification disagrees with its own problem statement.

title: Towards Formal Verification of LLM-Generated Code from Natural Language Prompts
claim: The authors explore deriving a formal specification of the user's intent from a natural language prompt so that it can be used to verify that LLM-generated code matches the intent.

take: Compare their route from prompt to formal intent specification with t's problem-to-specification step to see which checks a person could approve, since a person asking a question has no reference solution.

title: Scoring Verifiers: Evaluating Synthetic Verification for Code and Reasoning
claim: The paper proposes converting existing coding benchmarks into scoring and ranking datasets to evaluate the effectiveness of synthetic verifiers, with several metrics for different aspects of verifier quality.

claim: Building on pass@k analyses from RL work, the authors compare optimized agent harnesses with their pre-optimization counterparts to separate elicitation from expansion of what the model can do.

title: From LLMs to Agents in Programming: The Impact of Providing an LLM with a Compiler
claim: On 699 C tasks from RosettaCode across 16 models from 135 million to 70 billion parameters, giving agents a compiler cut syntax errors by 75 percent and undefined-reference errors by 87 percent for the tasks where agents outperformed the baselines.

title: RefineCoder: Iterative Improving of Large Language Models via Adaptive Critique Refinement for Code Generation
claim: Adaptive Critique Refinement lets a model refine itself from its own generated code and external critique, instead of imitating the teacher's code responses, and is applied iteratively to build the RefineCoder series.

title: KV Cache Recycling to Expand Usable Context Capacity in Low Parameter LLMs
claim: For small LLMs the authors recycle attention key-value states from one prompt to speed up a similar prompt, and observe consistent speedups when prefix overlap exists, no material change in output semantics, and baseline behavior when overlap is absent.

claim: The authors propose a numeric evidence evaluation method that assesses groundedness of LLM analysis of earnings call transcripts without relying on expert annotation.

claim: The first large-scale empirical study of floating-point usage across public GitHub repositories finds that benchmarks used in the literature are in some respects representative of real-world code but not in all.

claim: Detrimental semantic collapse, where all sampled programs fall into one behaviour cluster that is wrong, appears on over 3 percent of HumanEval tasks, 10 to 16 percent of MBPP and 18 to 32 percent of LiveCodeBench, and cannot be told apart from benign collapse without an oracle.

gap_note: Needs probe inputs per problem and a behavioural equivalence over t programs; the study uses large models and an LLM user simulator told the true intent, and cluster counts depend on the probe set chosen.

title: The Reliability Gap in Benchmark Auditing: Distribution Shift and Scale as Failure Modes of Contamination Detection
claim: Evaluating three contamination-detection paradigms across 25 models up to 27B, the authors report that across 335 evaluations only 201 yield correct outcomes.
quote: Across 335 evaluations, only 201 yield correct outcomes.
take: Before trusting any detector for the 32 contaminated problems, run it on known-contaminated and known-clean sets as the paper does and report how often it is right on dawnr's own splits.

title: Detecting Benchmark Contamination Through Watermarking
claim: The authors propose watermarking benchmarks before release and detecting radioactivity, traces the watermark leaves in a model during training, with a theoretically grounded statistical test.
quote: We introduce a solution to this problem by watermarking benchmarks before their release.
take: Watermark the text of any new held-out set before it is published so that later training on it by other models can be tested for, which a base model's prior exposure to MBPP could not be.

title: How to Run Statistics over LLM Judges and Trust the Results: Calibrated Inference for Small-Sample AI Evaluation with evalstats
claim: The authors find that running statistics over raw LLM judge scores inflates false positives, and that for many inter-rater agreement metrics false positive risk peaks at almost perfect human-LLM agreement.
quote: First, we find that running statistics over raw LLM judge scores leads to inflated false positives: counterintuitively, for many inter-rater agreement metrics, false positive risk peaks at "almost perfect" human-LLM agreement.
take: Where dawnr's judge scores support a comparison, apply calibrated small-sample inference and report the false positive risk of the judge before any significance claim.

title: IMU-1: Sample-Efficient Pre-training of Small Language Models
claim: IMU-1 is a 430M-parameter language model trained on 72B tokens that approaches the benchmark performance of models trained on 56x more data.
quote: We present IMU-1, a 430M-parameter language model trained on 72B tokens that approaches the benchmark performance of models trained on 56x more data.
take: Read its recipe ingredient by ingredient and pick the ones the pretraining study has not yet ablated for a small model, since sample efficiency decides what one RTX 4080 can do.

title: Effective Quantization of Muon Optimizer States
claim: The paper shows that Muon's update mechanism is uniquely compatible with a simple linear quantization scheme, bypassing the dynamic scaling needed for quantized AdamW, in an 8-bit Muon optimizer using blockwise quantization.
quote: Crucially, we show that Muon's update mechanism is uniquely compatible with a simple linear quantization scheme, bypassing the complex dynamic scaling required for quantized AdamW.
take: Try 8-bit Muon states in the local trainer to cut optimizer memory on the 16 GB card, and compare loss curves against full-precision states at equal steps.

title: SOAP, Muon, and Beyond: Pushing LLM Pretraining Scales
claim: The paper presents a unified empirical study of SOAP, Muon and AdamW using update-RMS matching to ensure fair learning rate transfer across optimizers.
quote: We then present a unified empirical study of SOAP, Muon, and AdamW using update-RMS matching to ensure fair learning rate transfer across optimizers.
take: Match update RMS across optimizers in the learning-rate and width experiments so that a comparison of optimizers is not a comparison of learning rates.

title: CONTRA: Discovering and Qualifying Behavior-Changing Questions for Selective Clarification in LLM Code Generation
claim: CONTRA is a training-free method that combines broad question discovery with semantic and execution-based question qualification for selective clarification in code generation.

title: Can Code Language Models Learn Clarification-Seeking Behaviors?
claim: Unlike prior work built around agents, the authors study whether a code LLM can be fine-tuned to learn clarification-seeking behavior itself.

take: Add rows in which the student asks which reading of an ambiguous problem is meant, with the answer drawn from the problem's tests, to see whether a small model can learn to abstain with a question.

title: Detecting Functional Memorization in Code Language Models
claim: Across 4 open-source models and 5 programming languages, 0.3 to 3.4 percent of filtered functions are counterfactually functionally memorized, reproduced with equivalent behavior in restructured code that textual metrics fail to detect.
quote: We find that 0.3-3.4% of filtered functions are counterfactually functionally memorized, i.e., reproduced with equivalent behavior in restructured code that textual metrics fail to detect.
take: Restructure benchmark problems by renaming, reordering and rewording, and test whether the student still reproduces the same behavior, to detect functional memorization of the 32 problems on which its clean answers concentrate.

title: A Rust-to-Lean Verification Pipeline with AI Provers: An Experience Report
claim: An experience report on a pipeline that takes production Rust cryptographic code to machine-checked Lean 4 correctness proofs, applied to Plonky3 field arithmetic, FRI folding and Horner evaluation and to RISC Zero Merkle inclusion verification.

take: Read its stage list as a reference for a route from a native C case to a Lean statement, to see which extraction steps the Lean lowering would need besides the proof search.

title: HELIX: Verified compilation of cyber-physical control systems to LLVM IR
claim: HELIX is an end-to-end verified code generation system for the intersection of high-performance and high-assurance numerical computing, compiling control computations to LLVM IR.
quote: This paper presents the design of HELIX, an end-to-end verified code generation system with a focus on the intersection of high-performance and high-assurance numerical computing.
take: Compare its treatment of numerical semantics through compilation with the statement-extraction step that relates flight sources to t, to see which obligations it keeps at the floating-point level.

title: Compositional Loop Invariant Inference for Multiphase Programs via Structured Neurosymbolic Reasoning
claim: CLOVER is a structured neurosymbolic framework for loop invariant inference on multiphase programs, evaluated on 316 linear arithmetic, 50 nonlinear arithmetic and 54 multiphase benchmarks.
quote: We present CLOVER, a structured neurosymbolic reasoning framework for multiphase invariant inference built on two interlinked mechanisms.
take: Split loops whose bodies branch into execution phases before asking for invariants, and request one invariant per phase, for the t programs whose loops contain conditionals that the Frama-C and Dafny backends find hard.

title: Ranking Function Generation with LLMs for Termination
claim: RAINFALL generates ranking functions for termination with a generate-verify-refine loop integrating LLMs with symbolic verification, evaluated on 358 terminating C programs and reaching 96.65 percent (346 of 358) when combined with PROTON 2.1.
quote: We propose RAINFALL, a neuro-symbolic framework which follows the generate-verify-refine paradigm and tightly integrates LLMs with symbolic verification.
take: Generate termination measures for t loops with a verify-refine loop in which the proof systems check the measure, instead of relying on measures found by a fixed hint list.

title: Proving Functional Program Equivalence via Directed Lemma Synthesis
claim: Directed lemma synthesis automates equivalence proofs between functional programs by discovering critical lemmas with program synthesis, using induction-friendly proposition forms that guarantee proof progress.
quote: This paper presents directed lemma synthesis, an effective approach to automating equivalence proofs by discovering critical lemmas using program synthesis techniques.
take: Use it for proving an answer equivalent to the reference solution over recursive data, where the inductive lemma is the missing step in the current equivalence check.

title: Quantitative Comparison of Credible Compilation and Verification In Coding Agent Compiler Development
claim: The paper presents the first quantitative comparison of the two primary compiler verification approaches, credible compilation (translation validation) and full verification, working with a verified compiler developed by a coding agent.
quote: We present the first quantitative comparison of the two primary compiler verification approaches, credible compilation/translation validation and full verification.
take: Weigh checking each lowering's output per program (translation validation) against verifying a lowering once, using its effort measurements as the comparison form for the seven lowerings.

title: Who Verifies the Builder? Toward Independent Assurance for Agent-Produced Software
claim: A verifier in a fresh context detected more of 46 seeded faults than the builder agent's own tests (Holm-corrected p = 0.006) and surfaced ambiguities in the specification, at the price of rare false oracles.
quote: a verifier in a fresh context detected more of the 46 seeded faults than the builder's tests
take: Write the Python solution and tests beside the question from a fresh context that has not seen the answer under test, and score both against mutants, so the reference is independent of the model that wrote the answer.

title: Disproving Program Equivalence with LLMs
claim: ProbeGen searches for counterexamples to the equivalence of two executable programs with a multi-turn LLM that sees prior probes and outputs; on a code synthesis benchmark it disproves 18 percent of samples that the benchmark's unit tests considered equivalent to the ground truth, with a human evaluation of its filter for spurious counterexamples.
quote: In a common code synthesis benchmark, ProbeGen disproves 18% of samples considered equivalent to the ground truth by the benchmark-provided unit tests.
take: Run probe search between each accepted answer and the problem's Python solution on the held-out problems, with a filter for counterexamples that violate the problem statement, to count answers that pass the tests and the gate but are not equivalent.
falsifier: Over the answers accepted as clean, if probe search finds counterexamples to fewer than 2 percent of those whose specification passed the Python-solution check, tests plus that check are already adequate.
gap_note: Needs deterministic executable code and an equality operator; probe generation by an LLM costs far more than unit tests, and the spurious-counterexample filter needs the problem statement and has imperfect precision.

title: Enhancing Program Repair with Specification Guidance and Intermediate Behavioral Signals
claim: SpecTune decomposes repair into suspicious regions connected by execution checkpoints and derives localized postconditions representing expected behavior at those points, attached to existing repair frameworks.
quote: SpecTune decomposes the repair task into suspicious regions connected by execution checkpoints and derives localized postconditions representing expected program behaviors at those points.
take: Derive postconditions on intermediate values of a failing t program from the problem's tests and the Python solution and give them to repair as the candidate signal, in place of the verifier's message.
falsifier: Give localized postconditions at checkpoints in the repair prompt for the failing cells of the diagnostic split; if the repaired count stays within 2 problems of verifier-message repair at equal request budget, the signal adds nothing.
gap_note: Postconditions are LLM-generated and validated against passing and failing executions of the buggy program; dawnr's failing artifacts are proofs and twin refutations, so checkpoint placement in t and validation against the tests must be defined, and the evaluation covers general repair benchmarks, not verification.

title: GinSign: Grounding Natural Language Into System Signatures for Temporal Logic Translation
claim: Existing NL-to-temporal-logic translation frameworks either assume accurate atom grounding or suffer from low grounded translation accuracy; GinSign grounds natural language into system signatures.
quote: While existing NL-to-TL translation frameworks have demonstrated encouraging initial results, these systems either explicitly assume access to accurate atom grounding or suffer from low grounded translation accuracy.
take: Ground the atoms of a model-proposed specification in the problem's signature (named inputs, outputs and helper functions) before translating, and score grounding accuracy apart from translation accuracy, using the same signature the type and scope schema enumerates.
falsifier: Count atoms in model-proposed t specifications that name something outside the problem's signature or supported helpers; if fewer than 5 percent of the replies lost at static checking (52 of 70) contain such an atom, signature grounding addresses too little of that loss.
gap_note: GinSign grounds atoms of propositional LTL with a BERT token classifier over signature prefixes, tested only on VLTL-Bench; t specifications are first order with arithmetic and sequences, so predicates, typed arguments and a training set of signatures with grounded atoms must be built.

title: NoTB: Oracle-Free Triage of LLM-Generated RTL via Cross-Model Formal Consensus
claim: NoTB infers correctness of LLM-generated RTL from cross-model formal consensus, showing that the diversity of model families within an equivalent cluster induces a calibrated correctness signal.
quote: We show that the diversity of model families within an SEC-equivalent cluster induces a calibrated correctness signal, enabling risk-coverage tradeoffs without requiring testbenches.
take: Test whether agreement among answers from different model families carries more evidence than agreement among seven lowerings of one answer, by comparing the two kinds of agreement against the tests on the same problems.

title: Evaluating Prompting and Execution-Based Methods for Deterministic Computation in LLMs
claim: The authors evaluate Chain-of-Thought, Least-to-Most, Program-of-Thought and Self-Consistency prompting on tasks needing precise error-free output: binary counting, longest substring detection and arithmetic evaluation.
quote: In this work, we systematically evaluate multiple prompting strategies, including Chain-of-Thought (CoT), Least-to-Most decomposition, Program-of-Thought (PoT), and Self-Consistency (SC), on tasks requiring precise and error-free outputs, including binary counting, longest substring detection, and arithmetic evaluation.
take: Compare execution-based answers against free-text prompting on exact arithmetic in the calculator fixtures, to confirm that the calc tool path is the one a small model should use for precise numbers.

title: Partial Contracts Suffice: Sound, LLM-Inferred Regression Verification
claim: The paper presents the first contract-based regression verification tool, inferring partial contracts with an LLM; on Frama-C-Problems it strengthens each inferred contract beyond what the caller needs and measures how much tighter it becomes.
quote: We present the first contract-based regression verification tool.
take: After a repair edits a program, check against partial contracts inferred from the earlier verified version that behavior used by callers is preserved, instead of reproving every obligation in all seven systems.

title: SpecRover: Code Intent Extraction via LLMs
claim: SpecRover examines efficient low-cost workflows for iterative specification inference within an LLM agent, built on AutoCodeRover and evaluated on the full SWE-Bench of 2294 issues.
quote: In this work, we examine efficient and low-cost workflows for iterative specification inference within an LLM agent.
take: Add an intent-extraction step to the repository agent's plan, stating what the change must preserve before editing, and check the final diff against that statement.

title: An Empirical Study on Influence-Based Pretraining Data Selection for Code Large Language Models
claim: The authors explore data-influence-score filtering for programming-related datasets and pre-train a 1B-parameter Code-LLM from scratch on 100 billion code tokens to test it.
quote: In this paper, we aim to address this gap by exploring the effectiveness of a widely used general data filtering technique, i.e., data-influence-score filtering, within the context of programming-related datasets.
take: Compute influence scores of training rows against the dev problems, drop the lowest, and train at equal row count to see whether influence-based selection beats the current family-balanced row set.

title: Verify Before You Distill: Prompt-Level Teacher Gating for On-Policy Distillation
claim: Teacher-Gated On-Policy Distillation admits dense teacher supervision only after teacher reliability has been verified at the prompt level.
quote: We introduce Teacher-Gated On-Policy Distillation (TGOPD), built on the principle that teacher reliability should be verified at the prompt level before dense supervision is admitted.
take: Record teacher reliability per problem and admit a teacher's rows for a problem only when its answer there has passed the strict checks, reporting how many problems each teacher is reliable on instead of one pass rate per teacher.

title: Language Models Can Benefit from Domain-Specific Inductive Biases
claim: The authors replace standard activation functions in transformers with learned splines tuned on specific datasets, as a simple way to modify inductive biases, and train small models from scratch on web text, code and mathematics subsets.
quote: We introduce variants of transformers in which standard activation functions are replaced with learned splines tuned on specific datasets, providing a simple way to modify their inductive biases.
take: Try spline activations tuned on a corpus of t programs in the small model and compare held-out t perplexity at equal parameter count.

title: ufakzeka-1: Building and Evaluating a 151M-Parameter Turkish Language Model from Scratch
claim: ufakzeka-1 is a 151M-parameter decoder-only Turkish model pretrained from scratch on 13.5B tokens of openly licensed text and instruction-tuned for chat, at about 286 dollars of cloud GPU, API and notebook time, with weights, data recipe, evaluation code and spend ledger released under Apache-2.0.
quote: We describe ufakzeka-1, a 151M-parameter (182M with embeddings) decoder-only Turkish language model pretrained from scratch on 13.5B tokens of openly licensed text and instruction-tuned for chat, at a total cost of about \$286 in cloud GPU, API and notebook time.
take: Use its spend ledger layout (tokens, hours, cost per run) as the format for dawnr's training budget record and its totals as a reference point for what a small from-scratch model costs.

title: RLVR Datasets and Where to Find Them: Tracing Data Lineage for Better Training Data
claim: ATLAS traces RLVR datasets back to atomic sources, attributing over 99.7 percent of 1.45M instances to 20 atomic sources, to resolve provenance collapse among overlapping datasets.
quote: To bridge this fragmented RLVR data landscape, we propose Atomic-source Tracing via Lineage-Aware Search (ATLAS), a systematic framework for tracing RLVR datasets back to their atomic sources, attributing over 99.7% of 1.45M instances to 20 atomic sources.
take: Trace the sources of dawnr's training and evaluation sets back to atomic sources to find problems that appear in several datasets under different names, since overlap between a source dataset and a held-out set is what leakage looks like at the dataset level.

title: Tokenizer Tokens Tell Training Tales
claim: The authors observe that tokenizers are trained on text and can retain traces of that text in their vocabularies, and formalize inference of such traces with a likelihood-ratio test under a threshold model of BPE inclusion.
quote: Tokenizers are usually treated as fixed preprocessing tools, but they are trained on text and can retain traces of that text in their vocabularies.
take: Apply the token-frequency test to the base models' tokenizers for benchmark text, as one more indicator of prior exposure to MBPP beside the 32 behaviorally contaminated problems.

title: A Deeper Look at Depth: Stable Generation Accounting for Quantifier Reasoning
claim: A generation-accounting change in Z3, justified by refinement from a confluent abstract solver model, reduces outcome instability by 94 percent on the unstable core of the Mariposa benchmark (55 of 60 queries, 99 mutants each by reseeding, assertion shuffling and variable renaming) without performance regressions.
quote: Our empirical evaluation demonstrates that our implementation reduces outcome instability by 94% in the unstable core of the Mariposa benchmark without leading to performance regressions.
take: Measure per-lowering outcome instability with Mariposa-style mutants (reseed, shuffle assertions, rename variables) of dawnr's own verification queries, and compare stock Z3 against the generation-accounting build wherever a backend uses Z3.
falsifier: On proofs whose result differed between repeated runs, including the SPARK relu_all twin, if mutants of each lowering's queries show outcome instability on fewer than 5 percent of queries, instability is not what costs verdicts here.

title: Tunable Automation in Automated Program Verification
claim: The authors present a mechanism giving fine-grained control over the availability of quantified facts in verification contexts, allowing developers to tune the level of automation.

title: RAIN: Agentic Proof Generation for Rocq-based Software Verification

title: SeVerus: Context-Aware, Gamified Benchmarking for Rust Verification
claim: SeVerus generates Verus benchmarks from six open-source projects by withholding lemmas into 819 quests comprising 10,095 levels, and reports that successful proofs rarely reproduce the withheld lemmas but use alternative decompositions.
quote: To capture this challenge, we present SEVERUS, a context-aware technique to generate Verus benchmarks that organizes verification tasks into quests, each divided into levelsin a gamified manner.
take: Build graded Verus tasks from verified project code by withholding lemmas at increasing depth, giving a curriculum of proof-completion rows with a verifier-checked answer at every level.

title: SEVerA: Verified Synthesis of Self-Evolving Agents
claim: Formally Guarded Generative Models let a planner LLM state a first-order-logic output contract for each generative model call; SEVerA is evaluated on Dafny program verification, symbolic math synthesis and tool-use compliance.
quote: We introduce Formally Guarded Generative Models (FGGM), which allow the planner LLM to specify a formal output contract for each generative model call using first-order logic.
take: Attach an explicit output contract (parses, well scoped, typed against the signature) to each model call in the answer path, with a fallback when the contract fails, so unmet contracts count as named abstentions.

title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Program Analysis, Part III: Mostly Harmless LLMs
claim: The authors note that analyzing only a small part of the program is often enough to show that a static-analysis warning is a false alarm, motivating LLM-assisted filtering of such warnings.
quote: Fortunately, analyzing a small part of the program is often enough to show that a warning is a false alarm.
take: Run CBMC on a small slice around a flagged call before building a full case, as a cheap filter on candidate findings, and record how often the slice already refutes the warning.

claim: PRECOCIAL automatically optimizes the programs that generate fully synthetic pretraining data, which until now were designed by hand, to accelerate downstream language-model training.

title: Compete Then Collaborate: Frontier AI Teachers Build a Verifiable Curriculum to Improve a Coding Student Beyond Imitation

take: Rank teachers by the strict execution-based checks per problem family before choosing which teacher fills which family; its teachers are Claude, Codex-GPT, Grok and Gemini, so its curriculum is a method to learn from and not training data for dawnr.

title: Provable Joint Decontamination for Benchmarking Multiple Large Language Models
claim: The authors formalize multi-model benchmark decontamination as a joint selection problem and propose Joint Envelope Conformal Selection, a conformal procedure controlling the global contamination rate under stated assumptions.

claim: Inference-time decontamination in proof-of-concept experiments reduces inflated accuracy by 22.9 percent on GSM8K and 19.0 percent on MMLU.
quote: Our proof-of-concept experiments demonstrate that ITD reduces inflated accuracy by 22.9% on GSM8K and 19.0% on MMLU.
