take: Sample candidate rows from several saved checkpoints of the student itself, score them on several aspects, and pass only candidates that clear the strict checks, so the data loop does not depend on an outside teacher for the selected rows.

title: The Valley of Code Reasoning: Scaling Knowledge Distillation of Large Language Models
claim: The paper studies the scaling trend of distilling competitive coding skills into two small non-reasoning LLMs, and fine-tunes at two distillation stages on the same data to separate learning phases.
quote: In this work, we study the scaling trend of distilling competitive coding skills on two small non-reasoning LLMs.
take: Plot the clean count against the number of distillation rows at several sizes to see whether a dip appears between the first gains and saturation, before choosing how many rows to buy.

title: SpecGuardBench: Can Coding Agents Construct Reliable Validation Harnesses from Natural Language Specifications?
claim: On SpecGuardBench, 291 tasks from 13 repositories covering 8 types of verification logic, none of four coding agents constructs a harness scored faithful for more than 63 percent of tasks.

take: Score a model-written native harness for faithfulness by running it against the original and the fixed source and requiring the expected verdict on each, the control that native_case already applies to hand-written harnesses.

claim: VeriBase automatically constructs software-verification libraries by jointly generalizing code and its theorems from successful verification solutions, treating them as declaration families harvested into shared interfaces.

claim: The authors enhance the training data for a code reward model with symbolic execution techniques to build a more comprehensive and objective dataset.

title: Tool-Guided Retrieval-Augmented Repair for Securing LLM-Generated C Code
claim: The workflow combines compilation diagnostics, CodeQL static analysis and KLEE symbolic execution with retrieval of prior repair patterns for iterative refinement of LLM-generated C code.

claim: Program instrumentation is proposed as a unifying verification paradigm with a clear formal correctness criterion, applied automatically, that can transfer witnesses and counterexamples back to the original program.

title: Finding Memory Leaks in C/C++ Programs via Neuro-Symbolic Augmented Static Analysis
claim: MemHint checks each LLM-written memory-operation summary with a Z3-based step against the function's control-flow graph, discarding summaries whose claimed operation is unreachable on any feasible path.
quote: A Z3-based validation step checks each summary against the function's control-flow graph, discarding those whose claimed memory operation is unreachable on any feasible path.
take: Check each model-written stand-in or function summary against the control-flow graph of the real function before it enters a harness, discarding summaries that claim effects no path can produce.

title: Where Should a Stuck Agent Spend Its Next Tokens? Causal Attribution of Inference-Time Resources
claim: BRA measures the marginal contribution of computation, information and feedback to repairing failed coding attempts on 194 function-level and 126 repository-level failures; task-relevant specifications consistently improve repair, public-test feedback gives small gains and retrieved code little or none, and three of four frontier models choose feedback in 95 to 100 percent of cases yet gain less than uniform random resource choice.

title: Evaluating Quantized Large Language Models for Code Generation on Low-Resource Language Benchmarks
claim: Seven-billion-parameter code models were tested on a consumer laptop at 2-, 4- and 8-bit integer precision and compared with non-quantized code models of 1.3, 2 and 3 billion parameters; performance drops significantly at 2-bit.

title: Anatomy of a Quantized Agent: VRAM Stability and Forecasting in Code-Synthesis Agentic Workloads
claim: Analytical models of peak VRAM decompose inference memory into weight-storage, KV-cache and activation terms parameterized by step count, tool invocations and context expansion, evaluated over 1,920 agent trajectories on one H100 with 4-bit quantized backbones.
quote: Analytical models of peak VRAM consumption for LLM inference decompose memory into weight-storage, KV-cache, and activation terms parameterized by step count, tool invocations, and context expansion.

title: Improving Code Generation via Small Language Model-as-a-judge
claim: The study examines supporting code generation with small models by generating several candidate solutions and having another small model select the most likely correct one, in the line of RankEF.

title: Scaling Lean Theorem Proving for Real-World Code Verification
claim: EasyProver, built from recursive agents with isolated contexts, asynchronous search and parallel tactic probing, uses an off-the-shelf frontier model with no additional training to prove 669 of 672 PutnamBench problems and to resolve 597 of 600 NTP4VC verification conditions and all 189 VERINA tasks by proof or refutation.
quote: Using an off-the-shelf frontier model with no additional training, it proves 669/672 PutnamBench problems and all six IMO 2026 formalizations and resolves 597/600 NTP4VC verification conditions and all 189 VERINA tasks by proof or refutation.
take: Let the Lean backend return a refutation as well as a proof for a goal, so the broken twin is refuted by search and not only by a concrete input, and log which of the two closed each goal.

title: PastaLean: Deterministic transpilation from Python to Lean for Verification
claim: PastaLean is an extensible system for deterministic translation from Python to Lean via the Python abstract syntax tree, with a type inference engine for untyped code, covering more than 92 percent of LeetCode and HumanEval+ and more than 98 percent of LiveCodeBench ground truth Python files.
quote: We present PastaLean, an extensible system for deterministic translation from Python to Lean via the Abstract Syntax Tree of Python.
take: Translate each problem's Python solution deterministically into Lean, with no model in the path, as an independent statement of the intended function against which the lowered Lean program can be compared.

title: crush: Extensible Proof Automation for Lean
claim: crush is an extensible SMT-backed proof automation framework for Lean, built because higher-order functions, inductive datatypes and user abstractions make it hard to translate proof obligations into first-order SMT queries and reconstruct kernel-checked proofs.
quote: We present crush, an extensible SMT-backed proof automation framework for Lean.
take: Try SMT-backed automation on the goals that the Lean lowering currently leaves to the model, and count goals closed with kernel-checked proofs and no model call.

title: Agentic Planning for Symbolic Execution
claim: Agolic is an agentic planning system that uses evidence from earlier runs to choose and configure later bounded symbolic execution runs; on every program it extends the branch coverage of continuous symbolic execution and covers more than 3x as many branches on average.
quote: We present Agolic, an agentic planning system that uses evidence from earlier runs to choose and configure later bounded symbolic execution (BSE) runs, which the underlying symbolic execution tool then carries out.
take: Choose the next CBMC run's unwind bound and options from the coverage evidence of the previous run, with the planner restricted to settings the assumption-coverage stage can audit.

title: Enabling Memory Safety of C Programs using LLMs
claim: The authors harness LLM capabilities for complex code reasoning and rewriting of large codebases to enable memory safety of C programs, evaluated on micro-benchmarks and real-world code up to 20K lines.
quote: We show how to harness LLM capabilities to do complex code reasoning as well as rewriting of large codebases.
take: Use model-proposed rewrites that make a flagged function's memory behavior explicit as a way to draft fixes for findings, and accept a rewrite only when the fixed-variant control passes.

title: Do Theorem Provers Need Theorem-Proving Agents? mini-Lean-agent: A Coding-Agent Baseline for Lean
claim: mini-Lean-agent is a deliberately minimal agent for Lean tasks whose only model-visible tool is bash, which solves 7 of 12 Putnam 2025 problems at a 2 dollar per-problem limit against 4 of 12 for AxProverBase, with Gemini 3.8 Flash as the base model.
quote: We introduce mini-Lean-agent, a deliberately minimal agent for Lean tasks whose only model-visible tool is bash.
take: Compare the repository agent's specialized tools with a bash-only configuration on the same tasks and a local small model, to find out whether the extra tool surface helps at this model size.

title: CodeI/O: Condensing Reasoning Patterns via Code Input-Output Prediction
claim: CodeI/O condenses reasoning patterns embedded in code by transforming original code into a code input-output prediction format, and reports consistent improvements across symbolic, scientific, logic, math and numerical, and commonsense reasoning tasks.
quote: To address this issue, we propose CodeI/O, a novel approach that systematically condenses diverse reasoning patterns inherently embedded in contextually-grounded codes, through transforming the original code into a code input-output prediction format.
take: Derive rows from verified t programs that ask for the output given the program and an input, or an input that yields a given output, as auxiliary execution-prediction rows next to the trace pilot, and check whether held-out clean answers move.

title: Compressed code: the hidden effects of quantization and distillation on programming tokens
claim: The authors characterize how programming languages are encoded in LLM tokenizers by analyzing vocabulary distribution and keyword coverage patterns, to examine token-level mechanisms in quantized and distilled code models.
quote: Through systematic analysis of programming language token representations, we characterize how programming languages are encoded in LLM tokenizers by analyzing their vocabulary distribution and keyword coverage patterns.
take: Measure the keyword coverage and tokens per construct of t in candidate tokenizers with this analysis, as a check on the tokenizer compression figures before choosing the vocabulary for a from-scratch run.

quote: On 9 SWE-bench Verified problems (45 trials, Claude Opus 4.6, temperature 0), CCV achieves perfect separation between contaminated and genuine reasoning (Mann-Whitney U=0, p approx 0.012, r = 1.0).
